c.tagline: Ancient walled river city of Teochew cuisine, gongfu tea and the floating Guangji Bridge.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis are cheap — most cross-town rides run ¥20–30. Didi is the main ride-hail app. Almost everything is paid via Alipay or WeChat Pay QR codes (both now accept linked foreign cards); carry a little cash as backup since Western credit cards are rarely swiped.

emergency.note: 110 is police, 120 is the ambulance/medical line, and 119 reaches the fire brigade.

hood_desc: The walled historic core, threaded by Paifang Street with its 22 restored stone memorial archways and by Jiadi Alley's Qing-era mansions; a warren of teahouses, snack stalls, ceramics shops and boutique inns — the must-stay heart for first-time visitors.

The eastern edge of the old town along the Han River, anchored by the Ming city wall, the Guangji (Xiangzi) Gate and the famous Guangji Bridge, a Song-dynasty span whose central section is a row of floating boats; scenic and photogenic, especially at dusk.

The northwest quarter around the 1,000-year-old Kaiyuan Temple and the willow-lined West Lake park; a calm, central area mixing temples, gardens and everyday local streets, walkable to all the sights.

The modern downtown around Chaozhou People's Square and its musical fountain, with malls, chain hotels, the city museum and wide avenues; the practical, convenient base with the most shopping and dining variety.

A quieter district southwest of the centre that is the engine of Chaozhou's world-famous ceramics industry, lined with porcelain factories, showrooms and workshops; local and low-key, good for buyers and browsers.

water.note: As across mainland China, drink boiled or bottled water rather than from the tap.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 6:00 AM to around 9–10:00 PM; after that, taxis and Didi are the way to get around.
transit.note: The compact old city is best explored on foot — most sights are within walking distance. Buses reach outer districts and the high-speed Chaoshan railway station (about 45 minutes); taxis are cheap for longer hops.
transit.pay: Bus fares (from ¥2) are paid by scanning an Alipay/WeChat Pay QR code, tapping a transit card, or dropping exact cash in the farebox. There is no metro; buses and taxis/Didi cover the city.

air: Jieyang Chaoshan International Airport (SWA) — about 35 km southwest, shared with Shantou and Jieyang
bus: Chaozhou Bus Terminal — intercity coaches to Shantou, Jieyang, Meizhou and Guangzhou

car.idp: Not valid (a Chinese driving licence is required)

train: Chaoshan Railway Station — high-speed trains to Shenzhen, Guangzhou, Xiamen and Shanghai (about 25 km from the old city)

transit.m: Airport shuttle bus to Chaozhou city (~1 hr)
Taxi/Didi to the old city (~45 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not expected or practised in China; there is no need to tip taxis, restaurants or hotel staff.
